correctness.rationale: Every perfect matching contains exactly one hub spoke s_i; deleting its incident rim vertex leaves an even path with a unique perfect matching, yielding N=2r+1 facets M_i. The rim-edge incidence sets S_j={j+2,j+4,...,j+2r} in facet index, and inverse-of-two relabeling identifies their nerve with the cyclic length-r interval complex B(N,r). All nonempty facet-simplex intersections are contractible. For each 3<=t<=r, cyclic length-t facet has free endpoint edge because 2(t-1)<N, and its upper Boolean interval removes in 2^(t-3) elementary pairs; different intervals are disjoint. Hence B(N,r) simplicially collapses to B(N,2)=C_N in N(2^(r-2)-1) pairs, giving P_r≃S1. Equivariant nerve (simplex intersections have fixed barycenters) and circular-arc model yield rotations degree +1, reflections -1 on integral H1, without asserting the collapse itself equivariant. At r=2, enumeration shows M2 is P2 plus exactly five edges and no new triangles, so M2≃wedge^6 S1 and inclusion primitive split; at r>=3 Vega Theorem 5.2 makes ordinary wheel matching complex a wedge of spheres in dimension ceil((2r-2)/3)>=2, thus simply connected and the map from S1 null. Purity of P_r dimension r and nonzero H1 precludes pure shellable/CM. Independently checked finite r=2..7 facet incidences, nerve equality and Euler 0; finite test alone cannot prove the uniform statement.

final_claim: For every r>=2, the simplicial complex generated by perfect matchings of W_(2r+2) is homotopy S^1 with dihedral orientation character; its facet nerve collapses to an (2r+1)-cycle in (2r+1)(2^(r-2)-1) elementary pairs. Its natural inclusion into the ordinary wheel matching complex is a primitive split H1 injection at r=2, but nullhomotopic for all r>=3.
